```{=html}
<div class="lx-interactive lx-cards" data-learn="a02" data-src="../assets/learn/data/07-cost.json ../assets/learn/data/a02-contracts-risk.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">One plant, four contracts, 200 simulated price years (seed 2025; real 2025 dollars)</p>
<ol>
<li>A 100 MW solar farm makes 210,240 MWh in a typical year; a buyer needs the same amount, flat. Five things change each year: the hub price, the shape (how much of it solar hours catch), output, basis (node minus hub) and the battery's margin.</li>
<li>With no contract, the solar farm's sales run from $3.9M (P10) to $8.2M (P90) a year, and the buyer's bill from $5.2M to $10.2M.</li>
<li>A fixed price settled at the plant's node leaves the seller only output risk ($5.8M to $6.3M); the buyer carries price, shape and basis ($6.8M to $8.6M).</li>
<li>Settled at the hub, the basis moves to the seller ($5.3M to $6.7M); the buyer's range narrows ($7.0M to $8.3M).</li>
<li>A shaped contract, a flat block at a fixed price, fixes the buyer's bill at $7.59M; the seller buys the hours its panels miss ($5.0M to $6.9M).</li>
<li>Tolled at $5.17 per kW a month, the battery pays its owner a fixed $3.10M a year, and its margin ($1.9M to $4.5M) moves to the buyer.</li>
<li>A price $5.00 above fair moves $1.05M a year from the buyer to the seller; who carries which risk stays the same.</li>
</ol>
<div class="a2-tables">
<!-- a2-table:start (written by _tests/learn/test_a02-contracts-risk.js --write; do not edit) -->
<table class="a2-static" aria-label="P10 to P90 of 200 simulated price years, seed 2025, solar farm alone, millions of 2025 dollars a year">
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Contract</th><th scope="col">Fair price</th><th scope="col">Seller's sales, P10 to P90</th><th scope="col">Buyer's bill, P10 to P90</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>No contract</td><td>–</td><td>$3.9M to $8.2M</td><td>$5.2M to $10.2M</td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed price, settled at the node</td><td>$28.69/MWh</td><td>$5.8M to $6.3M</td><td>$6.8M to $8.6M</td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed price, settled at the hub</td><td>$30.69/MWh</td><td>$5.3M to $6.7M</td><td>$7.0M to $8.3M</td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed price, shaped: a flat block</td><td>$36.11/MWh</td><td>$5.0M to $6.9M</td><td>$7.59M, every year</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<!-- a2-table:end -->
</div>
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, you draw price years, sign each contract and see both parties' ranges move, with a seed you can change.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-datanote"><svg class="lx-ic" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><path d="M12 11v5M12 8v.2"/></svg><ul>
<li>A teaching simulation: the plant, the buyer and the five drivers' spreads are illustrative, drawn independently from a seeded generator (seed 2025 here). A price year is one simulated year, not a calendar year and not a forecast.</li>
<li>P10 and P90 are statistics of the 200 simulated years: one year in ten fell below the P10 and one in ten above the P90 (percentiles as in toolbox <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a>).</li>
<li>Solar capacity factor 24.0%: <a href="https://www.eia.gov/electricity/annual/html/epa_04_08_b.html">EIA, Electric Power Annual, Table 4.08.B</a> (U.S. solar PV, 2025; October 2026), as in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a>. One price year: all dollars are 2025 dollars.</li>
<li>Left out: taxes, a party failing to pay, curtailment, capacity payments, renewable certificates, the battery's wear, and the hours inside each year.</li>
</ul></div>
```

::: {#explain .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="a2-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Power purchase agreement</dt><dd>A long contract to buy a plant's power, or its value, at a set price.</dd>
<dt>As generated</dt><dd>The contract covers whatever the plant makes, so the seller keeps the output risk.</dd>
<dt>Settled at the node or the hub</dt><dd>The price difference is paid against the plant's own node or a trading hub; the basis between them sits with whoever is not paid at the node.</dd>
<dt>Shaped</dt><dd>A fixed amount every hour: the seller fills the gaps at the market price, so it carries the shape.</dd>
<dt>Toll</dt><dd>The buyer pays a fixed fee to run the plant, here the battery, and keeps what it earns.</dd>
<dt>P10 to P90</dt><dd>The middle 80% of the simulated years: a stated spread, not the worst or best case.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Why contracts matter to lenders, and a naming trap</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Lenders size loans on the bad years.** A loan is repaid from the low years' revenue, so a narrower range can carry a larger loan. That logic stays at awareness level here (side shelf X5, upcoming).
- **Fair is not the market price.** Each contract here is signed at its fair price, so on average it moves no money. Real prices also pay one side for the risk it takes on.
- **A naming trap.** Resource studies often name levels by exceedance: their "P90" output is the level exceeded in 90% of years, this page's P10. Check which convention a study uses.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Seeds, sampling noise and linked drivers</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Seeded, so reproducible.** The same seed gives the same 200 years on any computer. A new seed gives other years, and the P10 and P90 move a little: that is sampling noise (K5's standard error).
- **Independence is an assumption.** Here the five drivers are drawn independently. In real markets a high-price year may also be a wide-spread year for the battery; drawing linked inputs, and global sensitivity, are Modeler lesson [M7](m07-monte-carlo.html).
- **Hours inside a year.** Each driver is one number per year. An hourly model would settle each hour, and lets the battery fill a shaped contract's evening hours.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
:::

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="a2-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="richer" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A fixed-price contract at a fair price makes the seller richer.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. It moves risk, not money: over the 200 years the solar farm averaged $5.92M a year with no contract and $6.01M settled at the hub, a gap of sampling noise.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="hubsafe" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Under a hub-settled fixed price, the seller carries no risk.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Output and basis stay with the seller: its sales still run from $5.3M to $6.7M (P10 to P90).</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="block" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Under a flat block at a fixed price, the buyer's bill no longer depends on the hub price.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact, in this model: the buyer pays $7.59M every year, and the seller takes the price and shape risk of filling the block.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="worst" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “The P10 is the worst case.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. With no contract, 20 of the 200 years fell below the P10 of $3.9M; the lowest was $2.4M.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="a2">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="highyear" data-answer="c">
<p class="lx-qtext">In price year 1 the hub averaged $68.14/MWh, the highest of the 200. Under the hub-settled fixed price of $30.69/MWh, what happens that year?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">The buyer pays the seller $5.00M</li><li data-value="b">Nobody pays: the price is fixed</li><li data-value="c">The seller pays the buyer $5.00M</li><li data-value="d">The seller keeps the high price</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>The seller pays the buyer $5.00M: the hub price over its hours is above the fixed price, and the contract pays the difference on every MWh it made.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="whichfixed" data-answer="d">
<p class="lx-qtext">Which contract leaves the buyer's bill the same in every price year of this model?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">No contract</li><li data-value="b">Fixed price, settled at the node</li><li data-value="c">Fixed price, settled at the hub</li><li data-value="d">A flat block at a fixed price</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>The flat block: the buyer gets the same MWh every hour at one price. Under as-generated contracts it still buys the hours the panels miss at the hub.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div id="a2-drill"></div>
```
